title: Israel begins its Rafah offensive and seizes the Rafah crossing
body:
Israel began its offensive in Rafah, in the far south of the Gaza Strip, on 6 May 2024. The operation followed the collapse of ceasefire talks mediated by Egypt and Qatar, and rocket fire from Rafah at the Kerem Shalom crossing on 5 May. Israel said its aims were to defeat remaining Hamas forces in Rafah and to secure the border corridor with Egypt and the Rafah crossing.

On 6 May the Israeli military ordered civilians to leave eastern Rafah for parts of central Gaza and Khan Younis. Israel struck Rafah at least 50 times that day and its forces moved into the outskirts and toward the Egyptian border; the IDF said 20 Hamas gunmen were killed. On the morning of 7 May the IDF captured the Rafah crossing. A further evacuation order for additional areas of eastern Rafah followed on 11 May. Several countries condemned the evacuation orders. Before the offensive Rafah held more than 1.4 million people, many of them displaced from elsewhere in Gaza.

Before the offensive the United States paused a weapons shipment and said it would not supply offensive weapons for an assault on Rafah. IDF spokesman Daniel Hagari replied that the army had what it needed for its planned missions. South Africa renewed its request to the International Court of Justice on 10 May, hearings were held in the week of 14 May, and on 17 May Israel told the court it had found 700 tunnel shafts in Rafah, 50 of which crossed into Egypt.
